Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failing test `testUnion()` checks if the union of two XPath expressions returns nodes ordered by document order. The bug report describes that the core union operation does not sort the result nodes according to document order, causing the string conversion of a union node-set to produce incorrect results.

Inspection in the `org.apache.commons.jxpath.ri.compiler.TreeCompiler.union(Object[])` method reveals it instantiates an object of class `CoreOperationUnion`, forwarding the expressions to it. The constructor of `CoreOperationUnion` merely calls its superclass constructor without further processing.

No direct code snippet for the core evaluation or node merging logic (`compute`, `computeNodes`, or similar) of `CoreOperationUnion` was found in the class, suggesting the class likely inherits or uses a default implementation to handle union operations.

Given the failure symptom (nodes not sorted in document order), the root cause is likely that the union operation combines the two node sets but does not sort or normalize them according to the document order before returning. According to XPath specification, the result node-set of a union operation should be sorted in document order, without duplicates, for functions like `string()` to work correctly.

The lack of sorting leads to incorrect node ordering, causing the string value of the first node in the union node-set (as per document order) to be wrong, thus failing the test.

None of the recent bug reports relate to sorting or union functionality, so they do not provide relevant insights.

Hence, the bug occurs due to missing or incorrect sorting of result nodes in the union operation implementation in the `CoreOperationUnion` class or the code that merges the node sets for union results.

The fix would involve implementing or correcting the sorting logic (and possibly duplicate elimination) based on document order in the union node-set computation method in `CoreOperationUnion` or its related helper methods.

---

Next, I suggest inspecting methods related to evaluation or computation of union results in `CoreOperationUnion` or overriding methods in superclass for proper merging and sorting.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
